text: 5.	On April 25, 1874, Annie Jameson, a granddaughter of the founder of Jameson Irish Whiskey, gave birth to X in Bologna. X was a mediocre student who showed little academic promise and failed to get admission at the University of Bologna. Working in a makeshift laboratory in the attic of his family's country estate, he conducted experiments with a device that seemed to produce and detect a phenomenon first theorized by James Clerk Maxwell and demonstrated by Heinrich Hertz. X’s experiments sent signals first across a room, then across his garden, then across a hill. In 1901 he successfully transmitted a single Morse-code letter S (three dots) from Cornwall, England to St. John's, Newfoundland using a solid-state diode detector invented two years earlier by Y at the Presidency College in Kolkata without giving Y due credit. ID X (10 points) and Y (10 points). ‎<attached: 00126690-PHOTO-2026-04-25-08-47-36.jpg>

6.	On April 25, 1915, Royal Navy ships coordinated their landings at X using Marconi’s invention and dropped off 16,000 soldiers of the 29th Indian Brigade and the Indian Mule Corps. Over the eight months that the unsuccessful campaign lasted, 1,358 Indian soldiers died. Their story was so thoroughly overlooked that the first serious book about it, _Die in Battle, Do Not Despair_, was published only in 2015. Subedar Gambirsing Pun led the Gurkhas in an assault on a ridge that, for 15 minutes, reached the heights overlooking the Dardanelles — the only moment in the entire eight-month campaign when Allied forces achieved their objective. They were then accidentally shelled by their own navy and forced to withdraw. On the other side, the landings were repelled partly by the extraordinary leadership of Y, a 34-year-old lieutenant colonel leading the 19th Division. He told his troops that morning, “I don't order you to attack. I order you to die. In the time it takes us to die, other troops and commanders can take our places.” Y survived the battle and we know him by a name he picked for himself that means “father of the _____.” ID X (10 points) and Y (10 points).
Answers: X=Gallipoli/Gelibolu, Y= Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
